profile_md:
## Kuehne Chemical Company, Inc. (Kuehne Company): investor profile

**Bottom line:** Kuehne is a family-owned regional chlor-alkali producer and the dominant merchant supplier of **sodium hypochlorite (bleach) to Northeast and Mid-Atlantic water utilities**. It *is* a bleach maker. Unlike Olin, KIK or Hasa, though, its bleach goes mostly to municipal drinking-water and wastewater disinfection. That makes a large share of its revenue (~65%, estimated) strict water treatment. The rest is merchant bleach for industrial, institutional, cleaning, textile and distributor uses, plus co-product caustic soda, hydrochloric acid, potassium hydroxide and hydrogen sold into general industry. No financials are disclosed, so every revenue and EBITDA figure below is an estimate.

### Business overview
Kuehne runs electrolysis (chlor-alkali) plants that turn salt brine into chlorine, caustic soda and hydrogen. The chlorine is reacted straight into high-strength sodium hypochlorite on site, not shipped as gas. In the company's words: "Kuehne is a producer of high strength sodium hypochlorite (bleach), caustic soda and hydrochloric acid liquids used primarily in water and waste water treatment... by far the largest supplier of sodium hypochlorite in the Mid-Atlantic region supplying bleach to many of the municipalities from Fairfax County, VA north into Massachusetts" (Stuff Made and Built in Delaware, 2020). It says it supplies disinfection chemicals to a region of "over 36 million people, about 11% of the US population" and calls itself a critical-infrastructure provider. The plants run 24/7/365.

### History and ownership
- **1919:** Carl Kuehne starts making bleach in a Newark, NJ basement for laundry use.
- **1960:** Peter Kuehne Sr. becomes President.
- **1966:** The company incorporates.
- **1972-1978:** A sister company, Linden Chemicals & Plastics (LCP), runs a chlor-alkali plant in Elizabeth, NJ. The relationship ended by 1978.
- **Acquisitions and new assets:** Marzahl Chemical Company in Kearny, NJ (1979, now HQ and main plant); Kearny Barge Company, set up in 1987 for water transport; Chloramone Corporation in New Castle, DE (1989).
- **New chlor-alkali plants:** New Castle (1998), Kearny (2015), and a brine treatment facility at New Castle (2020).
- **2019:** Acquired New Haven Chlor-Alkali LLC in New Haven, CT. That was a small GreenChlor-process bleach plant formerly tied to H. Krevit & Co. Its minibulk distribution business was sold separately to PVS Minibulk in November 2019.
- **Leadership:** Don Nicolai (company counsel since 1979) became President after Peter Kuehne Sr. died in 2003. Third-generation Zach Kuehne became President in 2022, and Bill Paulin is Co-President for administration and finance. A 2025 company presentation calls it a "private, woman-owned enterprise."

There is no PE sponsor, no debt rating and no public filing.

### Products and chemistries
All core products are **made in-house** by membrane chlor-alkali electrolysis:
- sodium hypochlorite at 12.5-15% trade strength, with a concentrated low-salt grade and the branded **PARAGON ultra-pure bleach**, a low-chlorate/low-bromate grade aimed at drinking-water specifications
- sodium hydroxide (caustic soda)
- hydrochloric acid
- potassium hydroxide
- by-product hydrogen, which is used partly as boiler fuel and marketed for fuel/industrial use

It holds EPA pesticide (FIFRA) registrations for its hypochlorite and delivers by its own bulk trucks. The barge subsidiary moves product in the New York Harbor area. It does not sell coagulants, corrosion inhibitors, polymers or service programs, so its water exposure is disinfection plus pH adjustment only.

### End markets and customers
The core customers are municipal water and wastewater utilities from northern Virginia to Massachusetts. Public bid records show Kuehne as the awarded hypochlorite vendor to:
- Fairfax Water (VA): 15% hypochlorite at about $0.75/gal in 2018-19
- Westchester County (NY): $1.61-2.05/gal tiered, extended through Dec 2026
- Greenwich (CT)
- various NJ, CT and Long Island water authorities

The company's own product page also lists healthcare disinfection, cleaning/sanitation and textile bleaching. Caustic soda, HCl and KOH go to water treatment for pH adjustment and also to general industrial, chemical, food and pharma users.

Estimated end-market mix of the total platform:
- ~38% municipal drinking water
- ~28% municipal wastewater
- the remaining third: general manufacturing, chemicals, food, healthcare/institutional, pool distributors and other

### Footprint
Three US production sites:
1. **Kearny, NJ:** 86 N. Hackensack Ave; HQ, chlor-alkali and bleach plant on the Hackensack River, with barge access.
2. **New Castle (Delaware City), DE:** 1645 River Road; chlor-alkali plant, Title V air permit AQM-003/00115.
3. **New Haven, CT:** 71 Welton Street; bleach plant.

Their location close to the NY/NJ/Philadelphia/DC metro areas is a real advantage. Bleach loses strength over time, is heavy and costs a lot to haul, so short, fresh delivery routes win municipal bids.

### Financials (all estimated)
- **Revenue:** No revenue is disclosed. Data vendors vary widely: Buzzfile ~$82.7M, Kona Equity ~$70.7M, Growjo $37.5M (Growjo's 78-employee count is clearly too low). The company has said it employs "more than 150 people" (Sweeney tour release), and Buzzfile gives ~200 across locations. At ~$550-650k of revenue per employee for an integrated small chlor-alkali producer, and with the 2021-2025 hypochlorite price run-up (winning bids roughly doubled from ~$0.75/gal in 2018 to $1.6-2.0/gal in 2025), **total revenue is estimated at ~$100M for 2025 (range $80-130M)**.
- **EBITDA:** Estimated at **~$15M (~15% margin; range 10-20%)**. The new membrane cells and self-supplied chlorine should support better margins than a pure bleach repackager. Power cost in PJM/ISO-NE and sales of co-product caustic at prevailing prices are the main swing factors.
- **Water share:** Strict US water treatment revenue is estimated at **~$66M**:
  - ~$60M of municipal hypochlorite
  - ~$5M of caustic to utilities
  - ~$1.5M of acid to water treatment

### M&A strategy
Kuehne has grown by opportunistically buying regional bleach and chlor-alkali assets: Marzahl (1979), Chloramone (1989) and New Haven Chlor-Alkali (2019). It then reinvested heavily in its own electrolysis capacity. No acquisitions since 2019 were found. It is more a potential **target** than a consolidator. Logical buyers include:
- hypochlorite/chlor-alkali strategics (Olin, OxyChem, Westlake, Hawkins, Univar/Brenntag)
- a PE-backed municipal-chemicals platform
- infrastructure investors that like its critical-infrastructure, municipal-contract profile

### Competitive position
Its moat is regional:
- captive chlorine, with no need to rail chlorine gas into dense urban areas
- hard-to-replicate hazardous-materials permits in NJ, DE and CT
- short delivery radius to the country's densest utility corridor
- a long record of winning bids

Competitors include Olin/K.A. Steel, Univar Solutions, Hawkins (limited in the region), PVS Chemicals, Borden & Remington, Miracle Chemical/Allied-type repackagers, and small on-site generation (OSG) systems that let utilities make their own hypochlorite.

### Risks
- The municipal bid cycle, with annual re-bids on price.
- Electricity cost exposure.
- Swings in the price of co-product caustic.
- NJ environmental-justice permitting (the Kearny site required an EJ Impact Statement).
- Safety and incident risk at urban plants.
- Utilities shifting to on-site generation or UV/chloramine.
- Family succession and governance.

### What is uncertain
- Actual revenue, EBITDA, capacity (tons/day chlorine), product mix and the municipal vs industrial bleach split. None of these are disclosed.
- The employee count: ">150" is company-endorsed, and vendors say 78-200.
- Whether any Maryland terminal exists (Growjo mentions MD operations; not confirmed).
- The specific trigger for the "woman-owned" designation.
